title: The US Doesn't Have One Power Grid #shorts
summary: The lower 48 run mostly on three interconnections: Eastern, Western and Texas (ERCOT), each synchronized at about 60 Hz.
sources: The lower 48 run on interconnections (Eastern, Western, Texas/ERCOT) that operate at a synchronized frequency averaging 60 Hz (US DOE Office of Electricity, Learn more about interconnections): https://www.energy.gov/oe/learn-more-about-interconnections

Supply must match demand for the grid to stay stable; transformers step voltage up and down between the power plant, long-distance lines and distribution lines; the Eastern and Western interconnections are linked to Canada's grid (EIA, Electricity explained: delivery to consumers): https://www.eia.gov/energyexplained/electricity/delivery-to-consumers.php

scenes.narration: The US doesn't have one power grid.
The lower {48|forty-eight} run mostly on three: the East, the West, and Texas.
Inside each one, everything spins in step: about {60|sixty} cycles a second.

data.source: US DOE · GRID FREQUENCY AVERAGES 60 HZ

scenes.narration: The East and the West even link up with Canada's grid.
Three grids, one country. So no, not one power grid.
